$comment: Reference/inspiration cards for the media showroom (/social/media). Curated by hand or by a session: sourceUrl is the canonical value (never hotlink competitor images — links rot and leak referrers); note says what to steal; thumb is an optional small local file under public/social/media/refs/. assetType comes from src/components/root/social/showroom/taxonomy.ts.

references.title: Thmanyah — ثمانية
references.note: The style north star — the maker of the house typeface. Minimal Arabic typographic lockups: one thought per card, Serif Display headlines, generous space, no decoration the type doesn't earn.

references.title: Thmanyah — نشرة أها quote card
references.note: Real card, saved locally: Zaki Mubarak on true education — one quote fills a lavender field, display-size Thmanyah type, highlight swipe on the closing words, black attribution bar, the 8 mark alone at the foot. The exact lockup our testimonial format descends from.

references.title: Thmanyah — the system, second color
references.note: Al-Aqqad on happiness, mint field — same grid, same type scale, new pastel. Two cards side by side prove it's a system, not a design: rotate the field color, never the layout.

references.title: Thmanyah — فنجان episode as pull-quote
references.note: Podcast promotion with no episode art, no guest photo, no play button — the strongest sentence from the episode IS the card, labeled بودكاست فنجان in the corner. Sell the idea, not the format.

references.title: Thmanyah — آدم longform card
references.note: The longform archetype: bold question headline, then a full paragraph set small and ragged on warm paper texture, one emoji finger as the only CTA. A whole argument on one slide — what our 1-slide decks aim at.

references.title: Thmanyah — highlight opens the card
references.note: Al-Jahiz on companionship, lavender again — but the highlight swipe sits on the OPENING phrase, not the close. The accent is a movable spotlight: put it where the quote's weight is, never in a fixed slot.

references.title: Thmanyah — نشرة إلخ, third masthead
references.note: Same quote system, different product: نشرة إلخ on a salmon field, living author (إيمان العزوزي) not a classic. One layout carries every newsletter masthead — the corner label does all the brand differentiation.

references.title: Thmanyah — fourth pastel, same grid
references.note: Al-Jahiz on nobility, yellow field, white highlight. With lavender, mint, and salmon this completes the proof: the palette is a rotation of quiet pastels and the type never moves. Our field-color tokens should rotate the same way.

references.title: Thmanyah — آدم list card
references.note: The longform card's structured sibling: three bold colon-led labels (الكبير/الوسط/الصغير), each with a short definition and a hand-drawn underline, on the same paper texture. How a listicle stays typographic instead of becoming boxes-and-icons.

references.title: Thmanyah — film-promo banner
references.note: The documentary register: black field, two collage film cards flanking centered white type (تابع أفلامنا الجديدة), the 8 mark inside the artwork. Proof the pastel system has a monochrome sibling for the cinema side of the brand.

references.title: Thmanyah — reel cover, label only
references.note: Interview frame (توصيات معيشية) with nothing but a corner label and the 8 mark — no caption band, no title card. The cinematic frame IS the cover; branding stays in the corners. The restraint register for our reel thumbnails.

references.title: Al Jazeera Technology
references.note: Arabic tech-media cards at volume: copy-centric graphics, strong typographic hierarchy, consistent brand frame — proof the template lane scales to a daily cadence.

references.title: Al Jazeera Tech — news card frame
references.note: The daily 4:5 news card, saved locally: archive photo, purple headline band in bold Arabic, source credit (رويترز), صورة أرشيفية label, logo top corner, social-handles footer. A brand frame strong enough to survive any photo underneath.

references.title: Al Jazeera Tech — same frame, next day
references.note: DeepSeek study card in the identical frame as the Qwen one — band position, credit bar, label, footer all fixed. Proof the frame runs at daily volume with zero per-post design decisions.

references.title: Al Jazeera Tech — person-led variant
references.note: Keynote photo of Tim Cook, headline band dropped over the subject's body, face kept clear — how the fixed frame flexes when the story is a person, not a product.

references.title: Al Jazeera Tech — text-led explainer
references.note: The no-photo escape hatch: ivory card, bold lead with one keyword in color, body paragraph, framed video still below, vertical brand strips on the edge. Their explainer format for stories with no picture — our infographic register.

references.title: Al Jazeera Tech — architecture variant
references.note: ArcelorMittal × Microsoft cloud deal: teal glass architecture fills the frame, purple band carries the whole story. Corporate news with no faces — the frame works when the only visual is a building.

references.title: Al Jazeera Tech — event-stage variant
references.note: Conference-stage photo (TechCrunch Disrupt) under the same band; the wordmarks in the background do the scene-setting, source credit says وول ستريت جورنال. Third-party event photography inside a first-party frame.

references.title: Al Jazeera Tech — two-person variant
references.note: Modi–Zuckerberg handshake, band placed low so both faces stay clear. The two-subject composition rule for the fixed frame: people above the fold, copy below it.

references.title: Al Jazeera Tech — data-table card
references.note: A raw DeepSeek benchmark table dropped into the ivory explainer frame, Arabic lead with Latin keywords (DEEPSEEK-V4-FLASH, CODEX) in bold. Proof a real data table survives at feed size when the frame around it stays calm — the reference for our metrics cards.

references.title: Al Jazeera Tech — cinematic hero
references.note: The page cover: android and drone in a cable-lit scene, logo centered in the negative space. Their one cinematic asset — everything else is frames and bands. What a higgs-lane hero should feel like for a tech brand.

references.title: Al Jazeera Tech — reel cover, demo style
references.note: Open-source story (DECIMEN QR file transfer) as a 9:16 cover: real phones on a desk, terminal UI visible, purple caption band over the demo. Screen-truth over motion graphics — exactly our register for product reels.

references.title: PowerSchool
references.note: The enterprise K-12 standard: corporate blue/green gradients, sharp geometric grids, polished teacher-with-tablet lifestyle photography. What 'authoritative' looks like to district buyers.

references.title: Classter
references.note: Asymmetrical layouts with feature-spotlight vector badges (Admissions, Billing, LMS) floating around a central hero — the module-ecosystem story told in one frame.

references.title: Gradelink
references.note: Small private/charter/faith schools: social-proof testimonial lockups plus plain UI screenshots — 'No Tech Skills Required'. Trust over polish.

references.title: Alma SIS
references.note: Modern minimal duotone — deep purple + bright orange, flat design, high contrast. Aimed at forward-thinking administrators; closest to our own restraint.

references.title: Classe365
references.note: Flat, high-contrast product mockups for tech-savvy private schools — UI screenshots framed as the hero, minimal supporting copy.

references.title: OpenEduCat / Fedena
references.note: The open-source pitch to IT directors: technical mockups, dashboard data-viz, cloud/security iconography. Speaks to the buyer who reads the architecture page first — our open-source story overlaps.

references.title: Meta Ad Library — school management
references.note: The live competitive feed: every active SMS ad on Meta, searchable by advertiser. Check before designing a campaign — see what the category is running this month.

references.title: Behance — social media design
references.note: Complete brand case studies and full social asset suites — for direction-setting, not single-card ideas.

references.title: Dribbble — social post shots
references.note: Bite-sized craft: color pairings, asymmetrical layouts, typography experiments. Best for stealing one move, not a system.

references.title: AdEspresso ads gallery
references.note: Curated real Facebook ads with conversion commentary — why a hierarchy or layout works, not just that it looks good.

references.title: Pinterest — infographic & grid layouts
references.note: A search engine for modular layouts and infographic structures — feed it a slide archetype name and mine variations.

references.title: Noon Academy — أكاديمية نون
references.note: Saudi edtech speaking Arabic-first to students and parents at Facebook scale: bright single-idea cards, colloquial warmth over MSA stiffness, teachers as recurring faces. The counter-register to our calm voice — steal the accessibility, not the volume.

references.title: Alef Education
references.note: UAE K-12 platform with ministry-grade trust signals: bilingual AR/EN mirrored posts, muted palette, real classrooms over stock. What institutional credibility looks like to a MENA education buyer — our B2B register.

references.title: Madrasa — مدرسة
references.note: MBRGI free Arabic e-learning: educational infographic cards at daily cadence, Arabic typographic hierarchy that stays legible at feed size. Proof Arabic copy-led cards scale — same thesis as our template lane.

references.title: Classera
references.note: The Saudi LMS incumbent: product-UI screenshots framed in brand gradients, award/partnership badges as trust currency. What schools comparing us have already seen — differentiate with restraint, not louder gradients.

references.title: Anthropic — og/social cards
references.note: The template lane's visual north star: type-led og cards, one accent illustration, Ivory/Clay/Ink discipline, no decoration the message doesn't earn. Steal the spacing and the one-accent rule; never the logomark (no implied endorsement).
